title: Align public catalog option identity with inquiry submission
requirements: Make the service_option_id published by GET /api/v1/public/catalog directly usable by POST /api/v1/public/inquiries. The published UUID string is the public opaque identifier; do not expose or accept the internal service option code as an alternative public identifier.

Preserve the current transactional snapshots, catalog availability checks, idempotency and token semantics. A valid public catalog option ID is accepted; an unknown, malformed or inactive ID returns the existing OPTION_UNAVAILABLE result without creating an inquiry, receipt or token consumption.

Update synthetic PostgreSQL integration coverage to fetch or use the public UUID option ID for a successful submission, and prove that the legacy code string is rejected with no mutation. Tests use isolated random databases only and never read a local .env or configured source database.
Do not add routes, migrations, catalog fields, compatibility aliases, secrets, runtime composition, frontend changes or external calls.
acceptance: A browser can submit exactly the option it received from the public catalog without knowing database implementation codes.
Invalid or legacy option identifiers leave public submission persistence unchanged.
Focused PostgreSQL integration tests, scope and whitespace checks pass.

shared_paths_approval.reason: Contract repair required for the public catalog and inquiry endpoints to interoperate using the accepted opaque option identifier.
